::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Which of the following conditions must necessarily be true?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1080569/which-of-the-following-conditions-must-necessarily-be-true), asked by [Jose Arnaldo Bebita Dris](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/28816/jose-arnaldo-bebita-dris) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2014-12-25; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Suppose that $\{A, B\}$ is a set of mutually exhaustive conditions, and that $\{C, D\}$ is another set of mutually exhaustive conditions.
>
> If the following implications are true:
>
> $$A \Longrightarrow C$$
>
> and
>
> $$B \Longrightarrow D,$$
>
> then which of the conditions $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ must necessarily be true?
:::

You have $B = \neg A$ and $D = \neg C$.  Therefore $A \implies C$ and $\neg A \implies \neg C$.  Hence $A \iff C$.  

But neither $A$ nor $C$ need be true.
